purpose: Propose a coherent story hierarchy for the complete supplied Day 1 scope using its exact transient narrative evidence and Python-owned structural authority.
authority_order: Treat scope_id, ordered unit records, evidence ownership and locators, deterministic choice ownership, and hard locks as exact Python-owned constraints.
Read the supplied evidence text, speaker, kind, source identity, and source locator to understand each story-facing unit before grouping it.
Group only supplied authority-bound unit IDs, preserve their complete order and ownership, and reference each unit exactly once.
Use temporary proposal_key values only to connect proposed beat groups to proposed major clusters. They are non-authoritative transport keys and will never become topology IDs.

An accepted proposal requires uncertain_unit_ids to be empty. Populate it with exact supplied unit IDs only when membership genuinely cannot be resolved from the supplied evidence and constraints; doing so intentionally fails closed for human correction.
hard_rules: Return a whole-scope proposal, not independent adjacent-gap classifications.
Do not cross deterministic choice, choice-arm, call-occurrence, call-site path, loop, sequence, lane, hard-lock, or scope boundaries.
Use evidence only to propose semantic grouping; Python remains the sole authority for membership validation and topology.
Do not output titles, summaries, characters, claims, graph nodes, graph edges, choice topology, requirements, effects, coordinates, locators, or authoritative IDs.
Do not invent unit IDs or evidence IDs.
forbidden: use filesystem, web, tools, MCP, private oracle, mockup, Gemini, Grok, or application authority
infer hidden material or repair missing authority by guessing
turn proposal keys into stable or authoritative identity
